html:
A pandemic that swept the Roman Empire from 165 to 180, in the reign of Marcus Aurelius. Troops returning from Lucius Verus's war against the Parthians probably brought it west from Mesopotamia.

The doctor Galen saw it and described fever, sores and a dark rash over the whole body. Most scholars have taken it for smallpox, though measles has also been suggested. Nobody knows the death toll. Guesses run from a few percent of the population to a tenth or more, which would mean millions of people.

The plague hit cities and army camps hard, just as the Marcomannic Wars began on the Danube, and Marcus had to recruit slaves and gladiators. It may have killed Lucius Verus in 169. About seventy years later the Plague of Cyprian struck again.
sum: A pandemic that swept the Roman Empire from 165 to 180, in the reign of Marcus Aurelius. Troops returning from Lucius Verus's war against the Parthians probably brought it west from Mesopotamia.
